title: Budgeting app
description: A web app where you can input all your habits and generate future transactions for any date range based on those habits.
details: I decided to make a budgeting app so I can know how much money I would have at any date. I faced challenges experimenting with different ways to do the cron jobs but I learned a lot.
takeaways: I learned a lot about which technologies would work best and had lessons learned about reverting if that technology doesn't work that well.

title: Beaming video
description: A transporter beaming video modeled and rendered in Blender, recreating an iconic sci-fi transition effect using green screen chroma keying.
details: It was a challenge making the table for the transporter and took a month to make it, but it was my first successful 3D model. I 3D modeled the table and mapped an image texture on top of it.
takeaways: I was very happy about my success making a transporter table that looks very realistic and successfully recreating a Star Trek beam transition from my bedroom to my therapy office.

title: Blob man video
description: A character animation of an animated 'blob man' with walking animations built inside Blender.
details: It took a lot of trial and error following Udemy rigging and walking-cycle tutorials perfectly, but the final animation result was highly satisfying.
takeaways: Very pleased with the custom Blob man character rigging and keyframed walking cycles.

title: Harry Potter currency converter
description: A wizarding currency converter for TI-84 Plus calculators that converts between US Dollars and wizarding coins (Galleons, Sickles, Knuts).
details: I made this cool Harry Potter app on my calculator in High School. I improved the user interface through different versions from a basic menu to a fully custom one (v7.3).
takeaways: Incredibly rewarding to compile and code custom menu systems within low-level graphing calculator environments.

title: Beautiful Mind app
description: A virtual reality spatial learning application featuring an interactive teleportation watch navigation interface.
details: Collaborated on the VR experience, contributing a custom smartwatch enabling users to teleport scenes. Solved user screen clarity by expanding the watch face UI on hover.
takeaways: Designed a creative spatial smartwatch system acting as an immersive portal—completely an original design choice.

title: My mega website
description: First complete personal portfolio which featured a diary, life timeline, a fancy dynamic navigation wheel, and an early budgeting calculator.
details: I kept improving my mega website and even connected it to a MySQL database, configured custom server cron jobs, and deployed it on GoDaddy hosting.
takeaways: Learned a massive amount about database schemas, backend routing, server administration, and why modern web frameworks are vital.

title: My custom built gaming PC
description: Assembled a high-performance custom desktop computer with specifications built for heavy graphics workload and 3D Blender modeling.
details: First time building a desktop hardware configuration. Troubleshot initial boot failures by tracing power supply rails to identify a loose pin connection.
takeaways: Taught me the complete architecture of hardware interactions, thermal dissipation, and matching bus speeds—like assembling high-tech lego blocks.

title: Galaxy Life
description: An immersive 3D space travel and planetary survival simulator featuring webcam-based face-tracking parallax controls and real-time physical calculations.
details: Developed as part of the Adelphi University AI Society Hackathon, Galaxy Life is an interactive space life simulation environment. By integrating Google MediaPipe's computer vision face tracking, the app dynamically pans and tilts the 3D cockpit perspective based on the pilot's physical head movements, creating a stunning glass-like perspective. The user inputs their height, weight, and age, and the physics engine recalculates their biological metrics—such as gravity, weight, jump heights, atmospheric density, and year-lengths—across custom-simulated planets and moons. I designed a highly intuitive, futuristic cockpit UI that won 1st Place for UI Design.
takeaways: This project demonstrated the power of combining AI workflows with 3D web graphics to build a highly engaging and responsive user interface. Working solo under strict hackathon time constraints forced me to design efficiently. A week after the hackathon ended, I attempted to overhaul the cockpit in an experimental 'starship-redesign' branch on my own time; while that branch ultimately failed due to complex mesh synchronization issues and was abandoned, it taught me invaluable lessons in scope management, modular refactoring, and maintaining branch stability.

title: Biking Forecast & Planner XR (Concept)
description: A high-fidelity mixed reality concept design and UI ride planner proposal for spatial HUD cycling environments.
details: Biking Forecast & Planner XR is an unrealized, speculative Extended Reality (XR) product concept and spatial UI design deck. The proposal overlays virtual parameters in physical spaces, allowing cyclists to theoretically swipe through virtual bikes inside their real room, tap mounting points to configure gear, and pinch-to-zoom routes on interactive spatial maps. It showcases a floating 7-day forecast timeline and an immersive VR Simulation Mode concept previewed by holding the bike's handlebars, complete with custom heads-up cockpit telemetry (HUD). This project exists solely as an interactive design system and presentation proposal.
takeaways: This conceptual slide deck explored the convergence of spatial computing, real-world telemetry, and gamified customization. Designing speculative mixed reality mockups taught me how to architect intuitive physical gestures—like swiping virtual models in a real room, pinching spatial tables, and gripping handlebars to trigger VR transitions. Balancing functional parameters (like accessory weight drag and ETA forecasts) with immersive user interfaces remains a key principle in my spatial designs.

title: Biking Forecast & Planner
description: A weather-aware, real-time cycling commute planner built with Next.js, Leaflet, and React. Calculates route suitability scores and estimated travel times by dynamically evaluating headwinds, tailwinds, precipitation, and temperature along the exact path.
details: Developed a dynamic weather-aware routing application for cyclists. By integrating Valhalla's routing engine and sampling meteorological data from the Open-Meteo API at multiple coordinates along the route, the system calculates segment-level aerodynamic drag (headwind/tailwind/crosswind) and temperature comfort penalties. It includes a custom smart departure convergence loop to adjust departure times based on wind vectors and travel speeds, commute profile management, weekly planners, and a weather-aware trip-packing gear list.
takeaways: Gained deep experience in geospatial mapping, custom polyline decoding, processing meteorological vectors, and caching API responses locally to survive rate-limits with mathematical fallback mock engines.
